title: Still local agent API
description: Authenticated commands operate on one connected browser session. Bone positions and scales preserve source-local units (imported FBX local positions may use centimeters); quaternions use x,y,z,w. pose.move targets use normalized editor-world meters in the Y-up, +Z-forward scene. Commands are never retried after dispatch. Use explicit UUID command IDs for idempotency and expectedRevision to protect concurrent edits. Revision tracks document, rig, and FPS changes, not playback ticks. Set expectedRevision when an operation depends on an inspected document.

transport.authentication: Bearer token from .local/agent/connection.json. Browser bridge obtains it from same-origin GET /bootstrap.
transport.errors: HTTP failures return {error:{code,message,details?}}. Job failures use the same error object. Disconnection or missing completion acknowledgement can produce an error with details.uncertain=true; inspect the scene before issuing a new mutation. Cancelling a running command remains pending until browser acknowledgement, or ends as an uncertain timeout if acknowledgement is lost.
transport.files: POST /files?name=<filename> with raw bytes returns {fileId,name,size,mime,downloadUrl}; authenticated GET /files/:fileId downloads; authenticated DELETE /files/:fileId removes a staged file uploaded by the calling session once no queued/running job or open scene references it (returns 409 FILE_IN_USE while referenced, 403 FORBIDDEN for other sessions). URLs are relative to the engine origin. Files referenced by retained jobs are protected from 24-hour auto-expiry. Unreferenced files expire after 24 hours; capacity exhaustion returns a useful error instead of removing referenced files.
transport.idempotency: Command identities are journaled for 24 hours. A restarted service never redispatches journaled commands; interrupted or unavailable results require scene inspection. Expired identities must not be used as automatic retries.

bone.description: Stable skeleton index is preferred. A name must identify exactly one bone; duplicate names are rejected.

pose.description: One local transform for every bone, in skeleton.inspect order. Quaternions must be nonzero and are normalized by the browser.

rotationDegrees.description: Local XYZ Euler rotation in degrees.

scene.inspect.description: Inspect the scene, current revision, timeline, selection, warnings, and available engines.

scene.new.description: Start a new scene. keepCharacter:true starts a fresh animation (rest pose, empty timeline) on the character already loaded, so there is nothing to re-import. Otherwise pass kind for a practice humanoid or quadruped. The current scene is saved in the library first.

keepCharacter.description: Keep the current character and start an empty timeline on it.

scene.import.description: Import a previously uploaded FBX, GLB, or supported project file.

character.swapLook.description: Dress the current skeleton in another uploaded FBX or GLB's meshes and materials. Bones, rest pose and every key stay unchanged; bones are matched by name and extra joints follow their nearest matching parent. Creates a new scene and archives the current one.
character.swapLook.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state with warnings.

scene.project.description: Read the complete editable project document.
scene.project.resultDescription: {document,revision} where document is the complete ProjectDocument.

scene.restore.description: Restore a complete project document after application validation; existing work is archived.
scene.restore.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state. Full project structure and embedded objects are additionally validated by the browser.

scene.save.description: Save browser recovery and export the current project to a downloadable local .still file.

scene.archives.description: List recoverable scene archives stored by the application.

scene.restoreArchive.description: Restore an application archive by its returned ID.

skeleton.inspect.description: Inspect stable bone indices, unique names, parent indices, local poses, and world positions.
skeleton.inspect.resultDescription: Skeleton inspection including bones and rest pose.

skeleton.rig.description: Add a heuristic starter rig to an unrigged model. Existing skin bindings are preserved.
skeleton.rig.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state including rig warnings.

skeleton.kind.description: Set the humanoid/quadruped/creature classification without replacing the existing skeleton.

pose.get.description: Sample the current animation at time or the playhead.

pose.set.description: Set a full pose or a batch of local bone edits, creating/updating a keyframe. Generated motion is invalidated.

pose.move.description: Move a joint toward a world-space target using the application's IK solver and record the resulting pose. IK uses the existing four-ancestor chain, or the follow chain when follow is set.

follow.description: Follow chain: the joint's whole chain (neck, tail, tentacle) up to where chains meet bends after it and the joint keeps its world aim. 0 is snaky (one smooth curve), 1 is robotic (stiff links, sharp hinges). Omit for the four-ancestor IK. Limbs always use the four-ancestor IK.

pose.move.resultDescription: Updated pose/key and revision. An unreachable target may only be approached.

pose.describe.description: Describe the pose at time (or the playhead) in character space: key part positions [right, up, forward] meters from the floor under the hips, elbow/knee bends, torso pitch/lean, chest and head yaw, foot heights, warnings (hyperextension, floor penetration), and the body-part names this rig resolved. Use this instead of raw quaternions to check a pose.
pose.describe.resultDescription: {time, frame, parts, angles, ground, warnings, bodyParts}.

pose.intent.description: Pose by intent instead of joint math, then key it. Actions apply in order in character space ([right, up, forward], meters, turned with the hips): turn {part, pitch, yaw, roll} rotates about body axes (torso spreads over the spine; hips keep feet planted); aim {part, direction} points a segment (upper arm, thigh, forearm, shin...); bend {part: elbow/knee, degrees}; reach {part, to|by, relativeTo?, pole?} uses two-bone IK for hands/feet; move {part: hips, to|by, plantFeet} crouches/shifts weight with feet pinned; lookAt {part: head, at}; mirror {from: left|right, limbs}; reset {part|"all"}; grip {part: hand, on: prop bone, along?} wraps a hand around a held prop the way the rig holds it, with a straight wrist (on the holding hand it rolls the hand about the shaft; with no pole it picks the elbow direction that keeps the wrist straightest; the other hand grips at meters along the shaft, negative toward the butt). hold {prop, at, toward, relativeTo?, spread?, hands?} is the way to pose a held weapon or tool: say where the point between the hands goes and where the working end points, and the engine places both hands, keeps the prop clear of the body, head, hat and floor (turning it up to 30°, moving the hands up to 10 cm or ducking the head if it must) and reports what it changed. After keying, run motion.carry so in-betweens follow the prop too. dryRun previews without keying.

part.description: Body part: hips, spine, chest, torso (whole spine), neck, head, left/right Shoulder, UpperArm, Forearm (alias Elbow), Hand, Thigh, Shin (alias Knee), Foot, Toe; quadrupeds front/hind Left/Right Upper, Lower, Foot; tail, tailTip. Exact bone names and indices also work. pose.describe lists what this rig resolved.

pitch.description: turn: degrees; + tips the top forward (bow/nod).

yaw.description: turn: degrees; + turns the front toward the character's right.

roll.description: turn: degrees; + tips the top toward the character's right.

direction.description: Named direction (forward, back, up, down, left, right, out, in, or combinations such as "forward-up" or "out-down") or [right, up, forward].

to.description: reach/move: target [right, up, forward] meters from the floor under the hips, or from relativeTo.

by.description: reach/move: offset [right, up, forward] meters from the part's current position.

relativeTo.description: Body part: hips, spine, chest, torso (whole spine), neck, head, left/right Shoulder, UpperArm, Forearm (alias Elbow), Hand, Thigh, Shin (alias Knee), Foot, Toe; quadrupeds front/hind Left/Right Upper, Lower, Foot; tail, tailTip. Exact bone names and indices also work. pose.describe lists what this rig resolved.

at.description: lookAt: a body part or a [right, up, forward] point. hold: [right, up, forward] for the point between the hands.

pole.description: reach on a limb: where the elbow/knee points (named direction or [right, up, forward]). Defaults keep the current bend, else knees forward and elbows back.

plantFeet.description: move/turn on the hips: keep feet where they were (default true).

keepOrientation.description: reach: keep the end bone's world rotation (default true for feet, false for hands).

pointer.description: aim: a bone carried by the part (a weapon or prop bone such as a sword held in the hand) to point in direction, instead of the part itself. Bones without children point along their own +Y axis.

on.description: grip: the held prop bone (such as a weapon carried by one hand) to wrap the hand around.

reverse.description: grip with the other hand: true takes the shaft the opposite way round to the holding hand's mirrored grip (palm turned over). Omit to pick whichever keeps the wrist straighter; the result note says which it used.

along.description: grip: meters along the shaft. On the other hand: from the holding hand (positive toward the tip, negative toward the butt); required. On the holding hand: slides the prop through it from its rest grip (negative chokes down toward the butt so a long weapon swings clear of the body). The note reports how much shaft sits behind each hand.

prop.description: hold: the held prop bone (for example "Pitchfork"), carried under a hand.

toward.description: hold: where the prop's working end points: a named direction ("back-up", "forward-down") or [right, up, forward].

spread.description: hold: meters between the two hands (default 0.3 on a 1.8 m character); the back hand rides just in front of the butt.

hands.description: hold: both (default when the prop is long enough) or one.

clear.description: hold: false keeps the exact request even if it cuts into the body, hat or floor (default true: the nearest clean variation is used and reported).

pose.intent.resultDescription: Keyed pose (unless dryRun), per-action results (IK error when out of reach), and the pose.describe report of the new pose.

review.metrics.description: Animator checks over the whole take (or start–end) at the scene frame rate: foot sliding while planted, floor penetration, floating or floaty jumps vs. gravity, single-frame pops, backward knees, off-balance slow moments, dead holds, plus contact spans, hips travel/speed, hand top speed and loop seam. Read this after every change.

review.sheet.description: Render a labelled contact sheet PNG of the motion so an agent can see it: evenly spaced frames (default 8 across the take), explicit times, or atKeys, from 1–3 body-relative views (default side + front). Every cell uses the same framing so travel and spacing read correctly; key frames are marked ◆.
review.sheet.resultDescription: Uploaded PNG {fileId, name, size, downloadUrl}, times and views. The MCP still_review tool returns it as an image.

keys.list.description: List authored keyframes; includePoses returns full local transforms.

keys.put.description: Create or replace a keyframe at time using the supplied pose or a sample of the current animation.

keys.delete.description: Delete one authored keyframe, subject to the application's minimum-key constraints.

keys.move.description: Move an authored keyframe to a new time.

keys.simplify.description: Reduce authored keys to important poses, retaining animation endpoints.

timeline.set.description: Set playhead, frame rate, or duration. retime scales authored times when changing duration.

view.set.description: Change viewport camera, overlays, editing tool, or selected joint.

camera.description: Exact camera coordinates; position-to-target distance must be 1.2–15 world units. Read camera limits in scene.inspect.

history.redo.description: Redo the most recently undone edit.

motion.run.description: Run an available local learned-motion or physics provider. The command remains active until completion or acknowledged cancellation.
motion.run.resultDescription: Updated scene state, provider metrics, and warnings.

motion.clear.description: Discard generated motion while keeping editable authored poses.

export.description: Export the scene as GLB, editable project, Unreal package, or viewport PNG to local staging.

targetSkeleton.description: Existing Unreal Skeleton for retarget=skeleton. Requires the original FBX to be imported in this session.

scene.rename.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state including revision.

clips.list.description: List animation clips embedded in the imported character.

clips.select.description: Load an embedded source animation by its clips.list index.
clips.select.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state including revision.

pose.reset.description: Record the character rest pose at time or the current playhead.
pose.reset.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state including revision.

motion.quickGround.description: Apply the existing procedural floor correction, not a learned motion model.
motion.quickGround.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state including revision.

keys.replace.description: Replace all authored keys atomically as one undoable edit. Supply at least two full poses and distinct times within the timeline.
keys.replace.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state including revision.

tracks.list.description: List tracks in bottom-to-top order, their keys, and the active track.
tracks.list.resultDescription: Track details or updated scene state.

tracks.add.description: Add and select a layer. Subsequent pose edits record only changed properties.
tracks.add.resultDescription: Track details or updated scene state.

tracks.select.description: Select a layer for editing. Use null for the base motion.
tracks.select.resultDescription: Track details or updated scene state.

tracks.update.description: Rename or mute a track without changing its keyframes.
tracks.update.resultDescription: Track details or updated scene state.

tracks.delete.description: Remove an overlay track. Undo restores it.
tracks.delete.resultDescription: Track details or updated scene state.

motion.carry.description: Bake clean in-betweens for a held prop: between the authored keys the prop travels on an arc around the shoulders and both hands are re-solved to hold it every frame, and wherever it would cut into the body, hat or floor or bend a wrist badly, it is slid, tipped or the elbows swivelled as one smooth bump across that span; planted feet are pinned too. Writes generated motion (authored keys stay editable; motion.clear removes it). Re-run it after editing keys.

prop.description: The held prop bone, for example "Pitchfork".

ground.description: Pin planted feet as well (default true).

motion.carry.resultDescription: Updated compact scene state plus carry {prop, frames, bothHands, nudgedFrames, nudges [{from, to, slideCm, tipDegrees, elbowSwivel}], worstCutCm, worstSinkCm, worstWrist {degrees, at}} measured on the final grounded take and warnings.
